answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake in an inlet registry before submitting jobs. If a fraud claim proves that accounts coordinated to farm rewards, the protocol slashes their stakes and pays reporters. Creating a thousand sybils then requires buying and immobilizing a thousand bonds, rather than minting names for free; the attacker risks losing real capital as the tide turns. A walnut-sized bond may not deter a wealthy attacker, so stakes should match likely gains.
